R260.note: Sanitization approach and policy (FORMATTING+BLOCKS+LINKS) are the right shape for preserving allowlisted rich text via th:utext, but the import package `com.googlecode.owasp.java_html_sanitizer` is wrong (the library's actual package is `org.owasp.html`), so the code as written would not compile.

R261.note: supports() correctly restricted to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken via isAssignableFrom, matching authenticate()'s cast; no other behavior changed.

R262.note: Fixes the off-by-one in write_field's own bounds check, but ignores that encode_packet (the actual call chain / contract target) passes the hardcoded MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY (256) instead of the real malloc(requestedCapacity) size, so the reported stale-capacity OOB write is still fully exploitable when requestedCapacity < 256.

R263.note: Length check before offset check correctly avoids unsigned underflow, then bounds offset+length against buffer.size() before subspan(); throws on invalid input rather than performing UB.

R264.note: Branches swapped exactly to match the stated contract: admins get Order::all(), non-admins get only their own orders.

R265.note: Parameterized query with SqlParameter/@Owner correctly replaces string concatenation; same query semantics preserved.

R266.note: Standard comprehensive XXE hardening (disallow-doctype-decl, external entities off, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA empty); no legitimate use of DTDs/external entities is implied by the case, so no functional loss.

R267.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) correctly bounds the read to the 16-byte field, matches contract's NUL-inside and unterminated-name cases, never touches flags.

R268.note: Length check before strcat prevents overflow while preserving normal short-filename behavior; oversized names now fail cleanly instead of overflowing.

R269.note: Replacing manual docmd() envelope building with sendmail() closes the injection: verified against CPython 3.13 smtplib source that SMTP.putcmd() raises ValueError on embedded CR/LF in mail()/rcpt() arguments, so a malicious failed_sender/notify_address now errors out rather than injecting commands; minor extra EHLO from sendmail()'s internal ehlo_or_helo_if_needed() is harmless.

R270.note: std::array::at() throws std::out_of_range for invalid slots, matching contract's 'rejected or reported'; Badge shape and valid-slot behavior unchanged.

R271.note: secrets.choice() correctly replaces random.choice(); token shape (32 alphanumeric chars) and downstream mapping/response preserved.

R272.note: Moves the '%...%' wildcard into the bound parameter rather than the query string, preserving identical LIKE semantics while parameterizing user input.

R273.note: Direct ping.exe invocation with array args, absolute path, and leading-dash rejection fully closes shell and option injection; but the added count range cap (1-100) is an arbitrary restriction beyond what closing the vulnerability requires and could reject previously-valid larger counts, though it is disclosed in the write-up.

R274.note: Allowlist dispatch of pre-compiled types is the only safe remediation for arbitrary runtime C# compilation (no viable sandboxing on modern .NET); this correctly removes dynamic compilation, but it fully eliminates the endpoint's documented purpose of letting an admin submit ad-hoc rule source, a legitimate-use loss that is disclosed openly rather than silent.

R275.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() canonicalization check correctly closes the traversal; but replacing lines 71-73 as shown drops the `fileName = TESTFILES_DIR + param` assignment, so the later success/error messages that reference `fileName` would silently print 'null' instead of the actual path -- not mentioned in the write-up.

R276.note: fsockopen with no shell invocation fully closes the CWE-78 vector, but it swaps ICMP ping reachability for a TCP port-80 connect check -- a materially different test (hosts reachable by ping but not serving HTTP on 80 will now report unreachable, and the raw ping output format is gone) -- presented as functionally equivalent rather than flagged as a behavior change.

R277.note: Re-enables signature verification with an explicit algorithm allowlist (HS256) and proper exception handling for invalid/malformed tokens; necessary secret-key introduction is the only way to fix this CWE and is clearly called out.

R278.note: calloc(count, sizeof(ProductRow)) performs the overflow-checked multiplication internally and returns NULL on overflow, matching the contract's allocation-failure/oversized-count NULL-without-leak requirement.

R279.note: th:text replaces th:utext, escaping the user-controlled note before rendering; no other behavior or signature change.
